Techniques Used: Analysis of isometry groups and algebras
Uniqueness proofs up to scaling and isometry
Data & Platforms: T(n, R) (Group of lower triangular matrices)
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Maximal Symmetry Rigidity: Establishing structural constraints on homogeneous Einstein spaces by proving that left-invariant metrics with negative Ricci curvature possess maximal isometry groups, thereby linking geometric stability to algebraic properties of the underlying solvable Lie group.

Algebraic Reconstruction via Iwasawa Decomposition: Reconstructing real semi-simple Lie algebras of non-compact type from their Iwasawa subalgebras by identifying the compact subalgebra as a maximal compact subalgebra within the derivation algebra, providing a geometric proof of uniqueness.

Geometric Invariant Theory Integration: Utilizing the correspondence between Einstein solvmanifolds and nilsoliton metrics on nilradicals to analyze the stability and classification of Einstein metrics, specifically examining the role of pre-Einstein derivations and conjugation by diffeomorphisms.

Faithful Isometric Embedding Construction: Demonstrating that simply-connected, completely solvable Lie groups with left-invariant Einstein metrics admit faithful, isometric embeddings into the group of lower triangular matrices T(n, R), affirming their realization as submanifolds of symmetric spaces.
Summary Description: Michael Jablonski specializes in differential and Riemannian geometry, focusing on the structural analysis of homogeneous Einstein spaces and solvmanifolds. His research integrates Lie theory, geometric invariant theory, and Ricci flow dynamics to classify left-invariant metrics on solvable Lie groups. Key contributions include proving the maximal symmetry of Einstein solvmanifolds with negative Ricci curvature, reconstructing semi-simple Lie algebras from Iwasawa subalgebras, and establishing faithful embeddings of Einstein solvmanifolds into symmetric spaces. His work provides foundational insights into the Alekseevskii Conjecture, the stability of Ricci solitons, and the algebraic rigidity of geometric structures.
